name: Familial Dysautonomia Type III
aliases: Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy Type III

criteria.description: Presence of autonomic nervous system dysfunction including blood pressure instability and impaired sweating
Evidence of sensory neuropathy with loss of pain and temperature sensation
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the IKBKAP gene
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Exclusion of other hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autonomic dysfunction, sensory neuropathy, and genetic confirmation of IKBKAP mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for definitive diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other HSAN subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autonomic instability with blood pressure fluctuations
Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes

common.symptomName: Impaired lacrimation leading to dry eyes
Recurrent pneumonia due to impaired cough reflex
Poor temperature regulation with hypothermia episodes

rare.symptomName: Corneal ulcerations due to decreased corneal sensitivity

laboratory: Reduced levels of IKBKAP mRNA in peripheral blood leukocytes
Abnormal autonomic function tests including sweat testing
imaging: MRI may show mild cerebellar atrophy in advanced cases
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the IKBKAP gene (chromosome 9q31)
other: Reduced or absent flare response to histamine skin testing

distinguishingFeatures: Congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis
More severe anhidrosis compared to Type III
More common in Ashkenazi Jewish population
Mutations in IKBKAP but different clinical presentation

redFlags: Severe autonomic crises with vomiting and hypertension
Progressive sensory loss leading to painless injuries
references: Axelrod FB. Familial dysautonomia. Muscle Nerve. 2004;29(3):352-363.
Anderson SL, et al. Familial dysautonomia: a disease with hidden symptoms. J Child Neurol. 2016;31(3):345-353.
